key_distinction: NVLink = INTRA-node (inside one server, GPU-to-GPU). InfiniBand = INTER-node (between servers, NIC-to-NIC).
MIG = hardware-level partitioning with full memory AND fault isolation. MPS = software sharing, NO isolation of either kind.
DCGM = health MONITOR (watches GPU temperature, errors, utilization). Slurm = job SCHEDULER (decides who gets GPUs and when).
DCGM = GPU telemetry/diagnostics (software health layer). Base Command = full AI training platform (job + data + lifecycle management).
TensorRT = OPTIMIZE a model (creates a .engine file for a specific GPU). Triton = SERVE a model (runs it behind an HTTP/gRPC API at scale).
DPU (BlueField) = infrastructure processor — handles network/storage/security. GPU = AI compute processor — handles matrix math for training/inference.
NVLink = the high-speed protocol/physical links between GPUs. NVSwitch = the switch chip that creates an all-to-all fabric so every GPU can talk to every other at full NVLink bandwidth.
Slurm = HPC batch job scheduler (training, MPI jobs, resource accounting). Kubernetes = container orchestrator (inference serving, microservices, stateless workloads).
BMC = hardware-level, OS-independent (works even when OS is crashed). DCGM = software-level, requires OS and drivers to be running.
BF16 has 8 exponent bits (same as FP32 — same dynamic range). FP16 has 5 exponent bits (narrower range, needs loss scaling in training).
Base Command Platform sits ON TOP of Slurm — it is an AI management platform, not a replacement for the underlying job scheduler.
MIG max instances on A100/H100 = 7. DGX nodes have 8 GPUs. Never confuse these two 'eights-adjacent' numbers.

Training = massive sustained compute (backprop, gradient updates, hours/days, GPU-intensive). Inference = lightweight per-request (milliseconds, often CPU-tolerable). Scale ≠ per-job intensity. Questions always specify a direction — read it carefully.

On-prem wins: data sovereignty, predictable cost for sustained workloads, no egress fees. Cloud wins: no CapEx, instant elastic scaling, pay-as-you-go. Exam questions ask about ONE specific advantage — read the direction.
DL ⊂ ML ⊂ AI. Deep Learning is the most specific (inside ML, inside AI). Options will flip this — always draw the concentric circles: AI is the outer ring, ML is middle, DL is the innermost.
